passages.text: I charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead, and in view of His appearing and His kingdom: Preach the word; be prepared in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and encourage with every form of patient instruction.
passages.sermon:
God is present.
Christ Jesus is present.
Christ Jesus will judge the living.
Christ Jesus will judge the dead.
Christ Jesus will appear.
Christ Jesus has a kingdom.
I give you this command before God and Christ Jesus.
Preach the word.
Be ready at all times.
Be ready when it is convenient.
Be ready when it is not convenient.
Correct people.
Warn people.
Encourage people.
Use all patience.
Use all teaching.
passages.original: Διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ μέλλοντος κρίνειν ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς καὶ τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ κήρυξον τὸν λόγον ἐπίστηθι εὐκαίρως ἀκαίρως ἔλεγξον ἐπιτίμησον παρακάλεσον ἐν πάσῃ μακροθυμίᾳ καὶ διδαχῇ

passages.text: For the time will come when men will not tolerate sound doctrine, but with itching ears they will gather around themselves teachers to suit their own desires.
passages.sermon:
A time will come.
People will not accept sound teaching.
They will want to hear what pleases them.
They will gather many teachers for themselves.
They will choose teachers who say what they want to hear.
passages.original: Ἔσται γὰρ καιρὸς ὅτε τῆς ὑγιαινούσης διδασκαλίας οὐκ ἀνέξονται ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισωρεύσουσιν διδασκάλους κνηθόμενοι τὴν ἀκοήν

passages.text: So they will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths.
passages.sermon:
Some people will reject the truth.
They will refuse to listen to it.
They will turn away from the truth.
They will follow myths instead.
They will accept false stories.
They will choose myths over the truth.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπὸ μὲν τῆς ἀληθείας τὴν ἀκοὴν ἀποστρέψουσιν ἐπὶ δὲ τοὺς μύθους ἐκτραπήσονται

passages.text: But you, be sober in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Timothy, a young Christian leader.
Paul gives Timothy clear instructions.
Timothy, stay sober in everything.
Be alert and self-controlled at all times.
Endure hardship.
Do not give up when you suffer.
Do the work of an evangelist.
Share the good news about Jesus Christ.
Fulfill your ministry.
Complete all the tasks God has given you.
passages.original: Σὺ δὲ νῆφε ἐν πᾶσιν κακοπάθησον ἔργον ποίησον εὐαγγελιστοῦ τὴν διακονίαν σου πληροφόρησον

passages.text: For I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul says he is already being poured out like a drink offering.
Paul means his life is being given up.
Paul says the time of his departure has come.
Paul means he will soon die.
passages.original: Ἐγὼ γὰρ ἤδη σπένδομαι καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῆς ἀναλύσεώς μου ἐφέστηκεν

passages.text: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul has served Jesus faithfully.
Paul says, "I have fought the good fight."
Paul says, "I have finished the race."
Paul says, "I have kept the faith."
passages.original: τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα ἠγώνισμαι τὸν δρόμον τετέλεκα τὴν πίστιν τετήρηκα

passages.text: From now on there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that day—and not only to me, but to all who crave His appearing.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul says a reward waits for him.
This reward is the crown of righteousness.
God will give this crown.
The Lord is the righteous Judge.
God will give the crown to Paul on a certain day.
God will not give the crown only to Paul.
God will also give the crown to all who love Jesus’ appearing.
passages.original: λοιπὸν ἀπόκειταί μοι ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης στέφανος ὃν ἀποδώσει μοι ὁ κύριος ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ δίκαιος κριτής οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐμοὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς ἠγαπηκόσι τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Make every effort to come to me quickly, because Demas, in his love of this world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing this letter.
Paul is in need.
Paul asks you to come to him quickly.
Demas has deserted Paul.
Demas loved this present world.
Demas went to Thessalonica.
Crescens went to Galatia.
Titus went to Dalmatia.
passages.original: Σπούδασον ἐλθεῖν πρός με ταχέως Δημᾶς γάρ με ἐγκατέλιπεν ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα καὶ ἐπορεύθη εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην Κρήσκης εἰς Γαλατίαν Τίτος εἰς Δαλματίαν

passages.text: Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is useful to me in the ministry.
passages.sermon: Luke is the only person with me now.\r\nBring Mark with you when you come.\r\nMark is useful to me for ministry.
passages.original: Λουκᾶς ἐστιν μόνος μετ’ ἐμοῦ Μᾶρκον ἀναλαβὼν ἄγε μετὰ σεαυτοῦ ἔστιν γάρ μοι εὔχρηστος εἰς διακονίαν

passages.text: Tychicus, however, I have sent to Ephesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing this letter.
Paul is in prison.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul has sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
passages.original: Τυχικὸν δὲ ἀπέστειλα εἰς Ἔφεσον

passages.text: When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing this letter.
Paul is in prison.
Paul asks Timothy to bring some items.
Paul left his cloak with Carpus at Troas.
Paul tells Timothy to bring the cloak when he comes.
Paul also asks Timothy to bring his books.
Paul especially wants the parchments.
passages.original: τὸν φαιλόνην ὃν ἀπέλιπον ἐν Τρῳάδι παρὰ Κάρπῳ ἐρχόμενος φέρε καὶ τὰ βιβλία μάλιστα τὰς μεμβράνας

passages.text: Alexander the coppersmith did great harm to me. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
passages.sermon:
Alexander is a coppersmith.
Alexander did great harm to me.
The Lord will repay Alexander.
The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
passages.original: Ἀλέξανδρος ὁ χαλκεὺς πολλά μοι κακὰ ἐνεδείξατο ἀποδώσει αὐτῷ ὁ Κύριος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: You too should beware of him, for he has vigorously opposed our message.
passages.sermon: Alexander the coppersmith did great harm to me.\r\nYou also must beware of Alexander.\r\nHe strongly opposed our message.
passages.original: ὃν καὶ σὺ φυλάσσου λίαν γὰρ ἀντέστη τοῖς ἡμετέροις λόγοις

passages.text: At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them.
passages.sermon:
At my first defense, I stood alone.
No one came to help me.
Everyone deserted me.
I pray that God will not hold this against them.
passages.original: Ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ μου ἀπολογίᾳ οὐδείς μοι παρεγένετο ἀλλὰ πάντες με ἐγκατέλιπον μὴ αὐτοῖς λογισθείη

passages.text: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message would be fully proclaimed, and all the Gentiles would hear it. So I was delivered from the mouth of the lion.
passages.sermon:
The Lord stood by me.
The Lord gave me strength.
God did this so that I could fully proclaim the message.
God wanted all the Gentiles to hear the message through me.
God rescued me from the mouth of the lion.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Κύριός μοι παρέστη καὶ ἐνεδυνάμωσέν με ἵνα δι’ ἐμοῦ τὸ κήρυγμα πληροφορηθῇ καὶ ἀκούσωσιν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη καὶ ἐρρύσθην ἐκ στόματος λέοντος

passages.text: And the Lord will rescue me from every evil action and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
passages.sermon:
The Lord will rescue me from every evil action.
The Lord will bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom.
Glory belongs to the Lord forever and ever.
Amen.
passages.original: ῥύσεταί με ὁ Κύριος ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔργου πονηροῦ καὶ σώσει εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐπουράνιον ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν

passages.text: Greet Prisca and Aquila, as well as the household of Onesiphorus.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this message.
Paul told Timothy to greet Prisca.
Paul told Timothy to greet Aquila.
Paul told Timothy to greet the household of Onesiphorus.
passages.original: Ἄσπασαι Πρίσκαν καὶ Ἀκύλαν καὶ τὸν Ὀνησιφόρου οἶκον

passages.text: Erastus has remained at Corinth, and Trophimus I left sick in Miletus.
passages.sermon: Erastus has stayed in Corinth.\r\nI left Trophimus in Miletus.\r\nTrophimus was sick.
passages.original: Ἔραστος ἔμεινεν ἐν Κορίνθῳ Τρόφιμον δὲ ἀπέλιπον ἐν Μιλήτῳ ἀσθενοῦντα

passages.text: Make every effort to come to me before winter. Eubulus sends you greetings, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this message.
Paul asks Timothy to come to him.
Paul wants Timothy to come before winter.
Eubulus greets Timothy.
Pudens greets Timothy.
Linus greets Timothy.
Claudia greets Timothy.
All the brothers greet Timothy.
passages.original: Σπούδασον πρὸ χειμῶνος ἐλθεῖν Ἀσπάζεταί σε Εὔβουλος καὶ Πούδης καὶ Λίνος καὶ Κλαυδία καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες

passages.text: The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.
passages.sermon: The Lord is Jesus Christ.\r\nJesus Christ is with your spirit.\r\nGod gives grace to all of you.
passages.original: Ὁ Κύριος μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματός σου ἡ χάρις μεθ’ ὑμῶν
